title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the stratification of the Deligne–Mumford ('MD') compactification of M_{g,ν} by stable dual graphs. A multigraph is G' = (S', Ã', σ, o) with half-edges Ã', a fixed-point-free involution σ whose orbits are the edges A', a genus map g': S' → N and marked legs I' → S'. The previous page states the proposition. Given a set C' ⊂ A' of edges, there is a unique (up to unique isomorphism) generization morphism G' → G. G is obtained by contracting every edge of C' to a point; the surviving edges B' = A' \ C' become the edges of G.

This page lists the properties.
(1) π0(G') ≅ π0(G), so G is connected iff G' is.
(2) For each vertex α of G, the fibre G'_α is a connected component of the subgraph G^! = (S', C'). It is made into a marked multigraph G'(α) as follows: the genus is the restriction of g' to S'_α, and the marked points are I'_α ⊔ B̃'_α. Here I'_α = I'|S'_α, B̃' = Ã' \ C̃', C̃' = Ã'|C', and B̃'_α = B̃' ∩ Ã'_α. In other words, the cut half-edges of non-contracted edges become legs.
(3) Stability. G' is stable (the MD condition 2g'_β + n_β ≥ 3 at each vertex) iff every G'(α) is stable. This holds because the valence plus marking count of each vertex β is unchanged: C'-half-edges stay edges, while B'-half-edges and I' become marked points. Stability of G then follows.
(4) Hence if G' is an MD-graph, so are G and all the G'(α).

Geometrically, this is the combinatorics of how the stratum of type G' sits in the closure of the stratum of type G. Locally it is a product over the vertices α of strata of type G'(α) in M̄_{g(α), n(α)}, which is the standard gluing/clutching description of the boundary. The next page counts the 2^{card A'} generizations, ordered like the subsets of A'. It defines the 'écart' card C' and identifies its maximum with the modular codimension.
errors: No mathematical errors. The implicit genus formula for the vertex α of G (sum of g'_β plus the first Betti number of G'_α) is not written on this page; it is presumably handled elsewhere. Stating that G is stable 'aussi' needs a small check, but it is immediate since the contraction of a stable graph is stable.

ideas.what: Generization (edge-contraction) morphism of stable graphs G' → G determined by a subset C' of edges; the fibres over vertices of G are connected subgraphs whose cut half-edges become marked points
ideas.modern_name: Edge contraction / morphisms in the category of stable graphs; boundary strata and clutching (gluing) morphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford (1969), Knudsen (1983); systematized by Kontsevich–Manin, Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1990s), Arbarello–Cornalba–Griffiths
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the 'structure à l'infini' / Teichmüller tower in general terms, but not this combinatorics explicitly

ideas.what: Stability of G' is equivalent to stability of all fibre graphs G'(α), and implies stability of G
ideas.modern_name: Stability preserved under contraction; boundary stratum closure locally a product of moduli of the vertex types

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard working-out of edge contraction for stable (Mumford–Deligne) graphs and the compatibility of stability with fibres. All of it is well known from the Deligne–Mumford/Knudsen and modular-operad literature. It is historically interesting only as Grothendieck's own independent formalisation.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 reads roughly '"contraction en un point". On a)' – i.e. 'On a)' begins an enumerated list of properties.
'le demi-graphe de G' fibre en α' is more likely 'le sous-graphe de G' fibre en α' ('s...-graphe' in the image).
'composante connexe du sous-graphe [?] G^!' – the word is likely 'sous-graphe' (or 's-graphe'); G^! is the subgraph with vertices S' and edges C'.
In the margin addition at the top, the image reads 'de G,' inserted after 'arêtes'; the sentence reads 'B soit l'ens des arêtes de G qui [ne] subissent [pas] ...' – partly illegible.
Line 'Alors G' est stable (condition de rigidité MD) ssi les G'(α) le sont' – 'satisfait la condition' is struck out and 'est stable' is inserted above.
